title: S&P Global US Manufacturing PMI (final, Sep 2026 data) — 09:45 ET, 15 minutes before ISM Manufacturing
source: EST: read verbatim off S&P Global's own calendar listing, pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/ReleaseDates?language=en, RE-FETCHED DIRECT BY THIS LANE 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 23,858 bytes) rather than carried from the proposal: 'October 01 ... 13:45 UTC S&P Global US Manufacturing PMI'. 13:45 UTC is 09:45 ET under EDT. Corroborated three ways on the same session's fetches: (a) the page's own stated rule, quoted verbatim — 'Manufacturing PMI: first working day' — and October 2026 opens on Thursday 10-01; (b) a REALIZED release of the same series at the same slot, from S&P Global's own press-release index (pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/PressReleases?language=en, HTTP 200, 92,883 bytes): 'September 01 2026 13:45 UTC | S&P Global US Manufacturing PMI'; (c) that release's own PDF, fetched direct (HTTP 200, 121,394 bytes), whose masthead reads 'Embargoed until 0945 EDT 1 September 2026 / 1345 UTC 1 September 2026'. Filed estimate on the standing schema gap, not on date doubt: market-events-data.ts defines no confirmed-source prefix for a private PMI compiler (CAL: is 'automated aggregator cross-ref' and this is the publisher's own primary), and this lane does not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Supersedes proposals/sp-global-manufacturing-pmi-2026-10-01.from-sp-global-services-pmi-2026-10-05.json, which read the same calendar row; the proposal and this fetch agree.
notes: READ IT, DO NOT TRADE IT — and this entry's value is that it OUT-OF-SAMPLE TESTED its services twin and returned a correction. The sp-global-services-pmi-2026-10-05 ledger measured the 09:45-10:00 ET window BELOW its own median on 9 of 10 instrument-days across two SERVICES release days and registered FT-sp-global-services-pmi-2026-10-05-1 on the ORDERING statistic (the 10:00 ISM window out-moves the 09:45 window in 3+ of 5 instruments; in-sample 4/5 and 4/5). Run on the three MANUFACTURING release days in the same 60-day bar sample (2026-07-01, 08-03, 09-01), the ordering statistic FAILS on 2 of 3 days (ISM wins 2/5, 2/5, 3/5 — 7 of 15 instrument-days) while the CONCLUSION survives: the 09:45 window's share of its own 09:30-10:30 hour is below median on 11 of 15 manufacturing and 9 of 10 services instrument-days (20 of 25 combined). The confound is the calendar, not the print — this final always lands on the FIRST WORKING DAY of a month (10-01 is also the first day of Q4), so its 09:45 window carries month-start flow that a raw all-sessions percentile misreads as a release effect. METHOD RULE THIS ESTABLISHES: never percentile-rank a first-working-day window against an all-sessions distribution; normalise within the day. And the information point replicates on independent data: the August 2026 revision was flash 53.2 -> final 53.9 (+0.7, both terms primary), which flipped the flash's own '5-month low' headline into 'unchanged at 53.9' — and it landed on 2026-09-01, the DEADEST of the three windows (SPY p3, IWM p0). Real information; the tape does not pay for it. One structural asymmetry vs the services twin: the FLASH carries a published consensus and the FINAL does not, so the only surprise-testable moment in this survey's month is 2026-09-23. Full ledger: docs/research/events/sp-global-manufacturing-pmi-2026-10-01.md.
